names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 19 iunie, «Sfântul Cuvios Paisie cel Mare».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 19 Ιουνίου, «Όσιος Παΐσιος ο Μέγας και θεοφόρος», with the rank word and the epithets left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 19. јун ст. ст., „Преподобни Пајсије Велики“ — Преподобни is the rank and comes off, and „Велики“ is **kept**, because §5 is explicit that it is not a rank but the epithet «the Great»: it distinguishes him and does not grade him, which is exactly what §6 says a form should carry. `foldchk.py` returns NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM for «Пајсије Велики» and also for the bare «Пајсије», so neither form would have folded and the choice between them was made on the rule and not on the fold — which is the opposite case to the day before, where keeping a by-name was what avoided one.

Read out of the name link behind his place in days.pravoslavie.ru's line for 19 июня ст. ст., «Преподобный Паисий Великий», with the rank word «Преподобный» left off, which is the whole of what the link adds to the line.

feast.note: The same menologion number this folder's three other venerated rows carry. Its index page id1707 lists two lives, life6781 and life1348, and both were read; each heads «День памяти: 19 июня» and names no other day.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 19 июня ст. ст. — «Прп. Паисия Великого (V).»
Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 19 iunie — «Sfântul Cuvios Paisie cel Mare»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 19ης Ιουνίου — «Όσιος Παΐσιος ο Μέγας και θεοφόρος»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 19 Ιουνίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. It is plainly the same ascetic the folder's Romanian row keeps on 19 June: the Egyptian, youngest of seven, disciple of Abba Pambo, who withdrew to the western desert and was buried there, and whose relics father Isidore later carried to Pisidia. saint.gr adds the birth year 300, which the folder did not have, and the page head «(300 - ;)» gives no year of death. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the life page.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 02.07.2026 (19. јун ст. ст.) — „Преподобни Пајсије Велики“

attestations.note: The day’s second entry. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of this wave is. The Julian 19 June is the same menologion number this folder’s other venerated row or rows carry, so there is no second day and no §4 note is owed. A YEAR OF DEATH WHERE TWO BOOKS HAD ONLY AN OLD AGE. The folder holds `birth` 300 `traditional` off saint.gr’s page head «(300 - ;)» and **no `death` at all**: that page says only that he died at a very advanced age, and doxologia gave no year of any kind. This book states one flat: „Преселио се у вечност 400. године“. `death` 400 to 400, display «400», basis traditional, the sentence in the note. The `birth` is passed back **verbatim**, note and all, because `upgrade.py` replaces the whole `dates` object and a field not retyped exactly would be a silent edit; its note’s remark that saint.gr gives no year of death is still true of saint.gr and is left standing. The two years together make a hundred, which is a lifespan this folder now implies and **which is written nowhere as a number**, and `map-span` is not at risk because the folder has no `locations`. WHAT ELSE IS NEW, IN A FOLDER THAT IS ALREADY LONG. „Мисирац по рођењу и језику“ — an Egyptian by birth **and by language**, which neither other book says. That his teacher took him „за саученика преподобног Јовану Колову, који и описа житије Пајсијево“ — as fellow-disciple of John Kolovos, who also wrote Paisius’s life. **The folder’s doxologia account ends «The account is signed by a humble John»**, and this book names a John who wrote it; the agreement is stated in the life as an agreement and **not asserted as an identification**, which is not a reader’s to make. `ls saints | grep -i kolov` returns four Russian surnames and no John Kolovos, so no folder and no row. THE FASTS, AND THE SEVENTY DAYS. „Често није окушао хлеб по петнаест дана, још чешће по недељу дана, а једном је, по сведоџби Јована Колова, седамдесет дана проживео не окусивши ништа“ — fifteen days without tasting bread often, a week more often, and once seventy days with nothing at all, on John Kolovos’s testimony. The folder had the week and the two weeks off doxologia and the twenty-one days before Christ appeared; **the seventy days are new**. These are durations of fasting and not dates. THE APPEARANCES, AND NOT ONE OF THEM IS A RELATION. The prophet whose book he particularly loved and often read appeared to him more than once; angels of God appeared often; and the Lord Christ himself appeared and said „Мир теби, возљубљени угодниче мој!“ — a saying the folder did not have, its other quotation being doxologia’s «My chosen Paisius, thou sufferest much evil for me». **`jeremiah-the-prophet` takes no row**: an appearance is not a relation, which is the Three Hierarchs ruling exactly, and the new paragraph writes «the prophet whose book he loved» without the name even though the folder’s older prose names him — because `related-floor` reads a prose name as well as a linked one and this paragraph has no need of it. THE DEMONS AS ANGELS OF LIGHT. „Имао је велику борбу са духовима злобе, који су му се јављали понекад онакви какви и јесу а понекад у виду ангела светлих“, and the servant of God was never once deceived or beguiled. New, and the one thing in the entry that is about discernment rather than about austerity. WHO CARRIED THE RELICS, AND THE NAME THIS BOOK PUTS ON HIM. doxologia has «the abbot Isidore’s men» and saint.gr «father Isidore» take the relics to Pisidia. This book says „преподобни Исидор Пелусиот“, Isidore of Pelusium. `isidore-of-pelusium` exists — and **takes no row**, because this is an identification made off a name in another man’s life, which is not an identification, and because carrying a man’s relics is not a kinship. **AND THE NAME IS WRITTEN HERE RATHER THAN IN THE PROSE, BECAUSE THE FIRST DRAFT PUT IT IN THE PROSE AND `npm test` CAUGHT IT.** The paragraph first read «… buried them honourably: Isidore of Pelusium, where the other two books had an abbot and a father of that name and no more», and `related-floor.test.mjs` failed twice on it — once for the forward row and once for the reverse — because the string is this folder’s display name exactly. **That is §6’s trap measured rather than guessed**: the folder’s own older prose names an «abbot Isidore» and a «father Isidore» and passes, and this book’s fuller form does not. The fix was §6’s — the name out of the prose and into this note — applied as a `life_replace`-only spec, `.tmp/sr-drafts/fix-06-19.json`, with the same change made in the day’s generator so that the generator still reproduces the folder, and this row then re-applied with `.tmp/sr-reapply-json.py`, which touches the json half only. Nothing was added to `scripts/related-floor-exclusions.json`. `types` UNTOUCHED, AND **`wonderworker` IS REFUSED**. `venerable`, `hermit` and `ascetic` are all there; Преподобни is the `venerable`; and **„Велики“ is not a rank at all** but the epithet «the Great», which §5 of this wave’s brief says belongs in the display name and not in `types` — the display name already has it. „Био је прозорљивац и чудотворац знаменит по свему Мисиру“ stands in the **body**, and a rank read off a body is not written, which is why `wonderworker` was refused on Niphon on 14 June and is refused here. There is no type for прозорљивац at all. No `office`, no `locations`. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse. THE DAY’S FOURTH ENTRY IS REFUSED FOR WANT OF A FOLDER. „Преподобни Јован отшелник“ — John the hermit, who struggled in the sixth century near Jerusalem, reached by his ascesis so high a degree of purity and power that the wild beasts obeyed him, and reposed in the Lord in deep old age in 586. **Two folders read like him and neither is he.** `john-the-hermit-of-crete` is kept by the Greek calendar on **7 October**, holds no dates, and is of Crete, not of the desert near Jerusalem; `john-of-jerusalem` has `office` «Patriarch of Jerusalem», which a hermit is not. `ls saints | grep -iE 'john-the-herm|john-the-anchor|john-of-jerus'` returns those two and nothing else. Ruling 3: named here, left out of every life on this day, and no folder from me — and the sixth century and the year 586 are written nowhere, because there is nothing to write them on.

hymns.text: Îngerul cel în trup, cununa călugărilor, omul cel fără de trup, locuitorul cerurilor, dumnezeiescul Paisie se bucură prăznuind împreună cu noi pomenirea sa, dând dumnezeiesc dar celor ce se ostenesc pentru el; pentru aceasta cu multă osârdie să-l slăvim.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfântului Cuvios Paisie cel Mare.

english.text: The angel in the flesh, the crown of monks, the man without a body, the dweller of the heavens, the divine Paisius rejoices, keeping the feast of his memory together with us, and giving divine grace to those who labour for his sake; wherefore let us glorify him with much zeal.

hymns.text: Ὁ ἔνσαρκος ἄγγελος, τῶν Μοναστῶν κορωνίς, ὁ ἄσαρκος ἄνθρωπος, τῶν οὐρανῶν οἰκιστής, ὁ θεῖος Παΐσιος, χαίρει τῇ αὐτοῦ μνήμῃ, σὺν ἡμῖν ἑορτάζων, νέμει τοῖς κοπιῶσι, δι’ αὐτὸν θεῖον χάριν· διὸ ἐν προθυμίᾳ πολλῇ τοῦτον τιμήσωμεν.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον (Κατέβασμα), ᾌχος δ’, Ταχὺ προκατάλαβε — the only hymn on the page of «Όσιος Παΐσιος ο Μέγας και θεοφόρος», and it names him

english.text: The angel in the flesh, the crown of monastics, the fleshless man, the dweller of the heavens, the divine Paisius rejoices in his own memory, keeping the feast with us, and gives divine grace to those who labour for his sake; therefore let us honour him with much eagerness.

hymns.text: Пустынный житель, и в телеси ангел,/ и чудотворец показался еси, Богоносе отче наш Паисие:/ постом, бдением и молитвою Небесная дарования прием,/ исцеляеши недужныя и души верою притекающих ти./ Слава Давшему тебе крепость,/ слава Венчавшему тя,/ слава Действующему тобою всем исцеления.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 19 июня ст. ст. — «Тропарь преподобного Паисия Великого», глас 1. The common troparion of a desert-dweller — «Пустынный житель, и в телеси ангел» — with his name set in it, printed first of the two troparia under his name.

english.text: A dweller of the wilderness, an angel in the body and a wonderworker wast thou shown to be, our God-bearing father Paisius: by fasting, vigil and prayer thou didst receive heavenly gifts, and thou healest the sick and the souls of those who come to thee in faith. Glory to Him who gave thee strength, glory to Him who crowned thee, glory to Him who works healings for all through thee.

hymns.text: Божественною любовию от юности распалаемь, преподобне,/ вся красная, ямсе в мире, возненавиде,/ Христа единаго возлюбил еси,/ сего ради в пустыню вселися,/ идеже сподобися Божественнаго посещения,/ Егоже неудобь зрети и ангельскима очима,/ паде, поклонися./ Великий же Дародатель, яко Человеколюбец, рече к тебе:/ не ужасайся, возлюбленный Мой,/ дела твоя угодна Мне,/ се даю тебе дар:/ о коем-либо грешнице помолишися,/ отпустятся ему греси./ Ты же в чистоте сердца твоего возгореся,/ прием воду и прикоснуся Неприкосновенному,/ умы нозе Его/ и, воду пив, даром чудес обогатися,/ болящия исцеляти, бесы от человек отгоняти/ и грешники от муки молитвою своею избавляти./ О преподобне отче Паисие,/ молю тя, да умолиши и о мне,/ якоже тебе Бог обетова,/ ибо от сих грешник первый аз есмь,/ да даст ми Господь время покаяния/ и простит мое согрешение,/ яко Благий и Человеколюбец,/ да со всеми и аз воспою Ему: аллилуйя.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 19 июня ст. ст. — «Тропарь преподобного Паисия Великого», глас 2. The second troparion the page prints under his name, and proper to him: it tells the vision, the promise of forgiveness for whatever sinner he prayed for, and the washing of the Lord's feet, and it closes in the first person singular.

english.text: Kindled from thy youth with divine love, O venerable one, thou didst hate all that is fair in the world and didst love Christ alone, and therefore didst settle in the wilderness, where thou wast granted a divine visitation. Unable to look upon Him whom even angelic eyes can hardly behold, thou didst fall down and worship; and the great Giver of gifts, as the Lover of mankind, said to thee: be not afraid, My beloved, thy works are pleasing to Me; behold, I give thee this gift, that for whatever sinner thou shalt pray, his sins shall be forgiven him. And thou, burning in the purity of thy heart, didst take water and touch the Untouchable and wash His feet; and having drunk that water thou wast enriched with the gift of wonders, to heal the sick, to drive the demons out of men, and by thy prayer to deliver sinners from torment. O venerable father Paisius, I pray thee, pray also for me, as God promised thee, for of these sinners I am the first, that the Lord may give me time for repentance and forgive my transgression, as He is good and the Lover of mankind, and that I too with all may sing to Him: alleluia.

hymns.text: От млада званию Господа твоего последовал еси усердно, блаженне,/ вся, яже в мире красная, Его ради оставив./ Крест твой на рамена взем,/ вселился еси в пустыню,/ и, тамо ангельски пожив,/ тело твое постом и молитвами изнурил еси,/ и многим путь был еси ко спасению,/ вся возводя к Божественней высоте,/ Паисие преподобне,/ отцев и постников твердое основание.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 19 июня ст. ст. — «Кондак преподобного Паисия Великого», глас 8. Proper to him: «Паисие преподобне, отцев и постников твердое основание».

english.text: From thy youth thou didst follow thy Lord's calling with zeal, O blessed one, leaving for His sake all that is fair in the world. Taking thy cross upon thy shoulders thou didst settle in the wilderness, and living there as the angels live, thou didst wear out thy body with fasting and prayers, and wast a way of salvation to many, raising all to the divine height, O venerable Paisius, firm foundation of fathers and of those who fast.

hymns.text: Житейских молв оставлъ,/ безмолвное житие возлюбил еси,/ Крестителю подобяся всеми образы,/ с нимже тя почитаем,/ отче отцев Паисие.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 19 июня ст. ст. — «Кондак преподобного Паисия Великого», глас 2. The second kontakion the page prints under his name; it is the common of a stillness-loving ascetic likened to the Forerunner, with his name in the last line — «отче отцев Паисие».

english.text: Having left the clamour of life, thou didst love the life of stillness, likening thyself in every way to the Baptist; and together with him we honour thee, Paisius, father of fathers.

birth.note: saint.gr: «Ο όσιος Παΐσιος καταγόταν από την Αίγυπτο και γεννήθηκε το έτος 300 μ.Χ.», with its page head «(300 - ;)». The page gives no year of death, saying only that he died at a very advanced age, and doxologia gave no year at all.

death.note: The Охридски пролог for 19. јун ст. ст. says „Преселио се у вечност 400. године“ — he passed over into eternity in the year 400. The folder had no `death` at all before this: saint.gr said only that he died at a very advanced age and doxologia gave no year. Nothing is derived from the two years together: the hundred years they imply is a lifespan and is written nowhere, and the seventy-day fast and the fifteen days and the week this entry gives are durations of fasting and not dates (5 October 2026).
